program.section_heading: Biology - Associate in Science for Transfer (ADT) - MAS768 (Cal-GETC)
outcomes: Be able to identify and explain fundamental biological concepts and principles on the molecular, cellular, organismal, population, ecological, environmental and evolutionary levels.
Apply knowledge of biological concepts to formulate questions and hypotheses for research and demonstrate ability to find, read, understand, and critically evaluate scientific papers.
Develop experimental skills and techniques used in laboratory and field research and use the scientific method to develop hypotheses, design and execute experiments.

missing_explained.why: not in the text; the catalog prints MATH-C2210 Calculus I: Early Transcendentals in its place (likely a common-course renumbering)

notes: Each 'Select one of the following' pair (BIO-60/BIO-60H, CHE-1A/CHE-1AH, CHE-1B/CHE-1BH) is an honors-twin choice printed with 'OR', recorded as one entry with an alternative inside the required block.
CHE-1BH (Honors General Chemistry, II) and MATH-C2210 are not in the closed list; recorded as catalog additions.
Catalog codes are printed with hyphens (e.g., BIO-61, PHY-4B); matched to closed-list codes BIO 61, PHY4B etc.

The page prints three headings: two for MAS768 (Cal-GETC) and one for 'MAS767 (CSUGE)/MAS768 (IGETC)', which may be a leftover from an earlier catalog version; the degree text names Cal-GETC as the GE pattern.
Total of 32 units is stated in the catalog ('Units: 32.00' and 'Total : 32.00'); the 60-unit figure is the degree total.
